data.gender_notes: Galiena is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Galiena is derived from the Latin word ‘Galienus’, meaning ‘healer’. This name was also used as a title for several saints, including St. Galen, the third-century physician and martyr. In the military context, Galiena can be interpreted as ‘soldier’s light’, signifying protection, strength, and hope in battle. The name Galiena carries the meaning “Healer, Soldier's Light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Galiena usually hope their child will grow to embody healer, soldier's light and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Γαλιήνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Γαλιήνα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'Γαληνός' που σημαίνει σωτήρας ή λυτρωτής. Το όνομα συνδέεται έντονα με την έννοια της σωτηρίας και της λύτρωσης που βρίσκονται στο κέντρο της χριστιανικής παράδοσης. Η χρήση του ονόματος αυτού ήταν διαδεδομένη στην αρχαία Εκκλησία και συμβολίζει την ιδέα της πνευματικής σωτηρίας.

historical_references.reference: Galiena was the name of a famous Christian healer who lived during the late Roman Empire, around 160-200 AD. She was venerated as a saint in the Middle Ages and is now considered a patron saint of healers and physicians.

Saint Galiena of Perugia was a Christian martyr who lived during the 3rd century AD in Umbria, Italy. She is said to have been a virgin, a healer, and a midwife who was tortured and executed for refusing to renounce her faith during the Roman persecutions.
